# Diagnostic codes

Every mistake the loader finds is a diagnostic with a stable code, the file, line and column, the definition and the JSON path (04 §8.2). `clash-tools explain <code>` prints the explanation of one. A code is a letter for its usual severity and four digits; the first two group them: `00` mods and profiles, `01` files and syntax, `02` values and fields, `03` the keys every definition carries, `04` merging, `05` references, `06` expressions, `07` a type's own checks, `08` whole-set checks, `09` lenient loading.

<a id="e0001"></a>
## E0001 — A `mod.json` or profile file is missing, or a field in it is wrong.

*error, mods stage.* A mod is a directory with a `mod.json` (04 §3.2). The file must be one JSON object with at least an `id`. Each field has a fixed form: `requires` is a list of mod ids or of objects with `id` and `version`; `after`, `conflicts`, `imports`, `authors` and `experimental` are lists of strings. A profile (04 §3.3) is one object with an `id` and a list of `mods`. The message says which field is wrong and what was expected.

<a id="e0002"></a>
## E0002 — A mod id does not have the required form.

*error, mods stage.* A mod's id is its namespace (04 §3.2, §4.1). It starts with a lowercase letter and holds only lowercase letters, digits and underscores. The namespace `engine` is reserved for the engine and cannot be a mod's id; nor can the namespaces the engine keeps its own settings in, which are named after its subsystems (04 §10).

<a id="e0003"></a>
## E0003 — Two mod directories declare the same id.

*error, mods stage.* Each mod id may be found once in a search directory. Two directories in one search directory that declare the same id would make the result depend on which is read first, so neither is preferred: rename or remove one. (A mod found in an earlier search directory hides one with the same id in a later directory; that is reported as W0011, not as this error.)

<a id="e0004"></a>
## E0004 — A mod that is needed is not present.

*error, mods stage.* Every mod named in a profile's `mods` must be found in the search directories, and every mod in a mod's `requires` must be in the same profile (04 §3.2, §3.4). A profile is the whole list of what a game is made of, so a required mod is never added silently: add it to the profile's `mods`, or install it.

<a id="e0005"></a>
## E0005 — A mod or the engine is not of a version another mod asks for.

*error, mods stage.* `"requires": [{ "id": "core", "version": ">=0.1" }]` asks for a version of another mod, and `"engine": ">=0.1"` for a version of the engine. A requirement is one or more comparisons separated by commas, each `>=`, `>`, `<=`, `<` or `=` and a version. Versions compare number by number, and a missing number counts as zero.

<a id="e0006"></a>
## E0006 — Two mods that may not be loaded together are both in the profile.

*error, mods stage.* A mod lists in `conflicts` the mods it cannot be loaded alongside (04 §3.2). Remove one of the two from the profile.

<a id="e0007"></a>
## E0007 — Mods depend on each other in a circle.

*error, mods stage.* Everything in a mod's `requires`, and every present mod in its `after`, is loaded before it (04 §3.4). If following those links comes back to where it started there is no order that satisfies them all. The message names the mods in the circle; one of them must stop naming the next.

<a id="e0008"></a>
## E0008 — A profile cannot be found or names something that does not exist.

*error, mods stage.* A profile is looked for by file path, or by name in `profiles/<name>.json` beside the mods directory and in the `profiles/` directory of each mod (04 §3.3). The message says what was looked for and where.

<a id="e0009"></a>
## E0009 — A version or a version requirement is not written correctly.

*error, mods stage.* A version is numbers separated by dots: `0.3.0`, `1.2`. A requirement is one or more comparisons separated by commas: `>=0.1`, `>=1.0, <2.0`, `=0.3.0`. A bare version means exactly that version.

<a id="e0101"></a>
## E0101 — A file is not valid JSON.

*error, syntax stage.* The text could not be read as JSON. The caret is at the first character that makes no sense. Common causes: a comma after the last element of a list or object, a missing comma between elements, a key without quotation marks, single quotation marks, a `//` or `/* */` comment (write a comment as a member with the key "//"), a quantity written without quotation marks (`250 ms` must be `"250 ms"`). Nothing after the first syntax error in a file is read, so fixing it may reveal more.

<a id="e0102"></a>
## E0102 — The same key appears twice in one object.

*error, syntax stage.* JSON does not say which of two members with the same key counts, and tools disagree. The loader keeps the first and reports the second. Remove one. The comment key "//" is the exception and may be repeated.

<a id="e0103"></a>
## E0103 — A file is larger than the loader will read.

*error, syntax stage.* Loading has a limit on file size so that a malformed file cannot exhaust memory (04 §15). Split the file: a mod may have any number of data files in any directory structure.

<a id="e0104"></a>
## E0104 — Lists and objects are nested deeper than the loader allows.

*error, syntax stage.* Loading has a limit on nesting depth so that a malformed file cannot exhaust the stack (04 §15). No definition needs nesting this deep; look for an unclosed bracket repeated by a generator.

<a id="e0105"></a>
## E0105 — The mods hold more definitions than the loader allows.

*error, structure stage.* Loading has a limit on the number of definitions (04 §15), and each definition type has as many ids as its dense id is wide: a type whose ids are sixteen bits holds 65,536 definitions. The message says which limit was reached.

<a id="e0106"></a>
## E0106 — A file or directory could not be read.

*error, syntax stage.* The operating system refused to open a file or list a directory, or the file is not UTF-8 text. The message carries the system's reason. Check that the path exists, that it can be read, and that the file is saved as UTF-8.

<a id="e0107"></a>
## E0107 — A data file holds something that is not a definition.

*error, structure stage.* A data file is a JSON list of objects, or a single object (04 §5). Each object is one definition. A string, a number or a nested list in that position is not.

<a id="e0201"></a>
## E0201 — A value is of the wrong kind for its field.

*error, typed load stage.* The field expects one kind of JSON value and was given another: a string where a number belongs, a number where a list belongs. The message says what was expected and what was found. Remember that a quantity with a unit is a string (`"70 kPa"`) and a bare number is in SI units.

<a id="e0202"></a>
## E0202 — A required field is missing.

*error, typed load stage.* The definition type requires this field and gives it no default. Add it. If the definition uses `copy_from`, the field must be present in the parent or in the definition itself. The caret points at the object that should hold the field.

<a id="e0203"></a>
## E0203 — A key is not one the definition type knows.

*error, typed load stage.* Unknown keys are errors (04 §5), because a misspelt key would otherwise be silently ignored and the field would keep its default. If a known key is close to the one written, the diagnostic suggests it. To leave a note in a definition, use the comment key "//".

<a id="e0204"></a>
## E0204 — A quantity is not a number followed by a known unit.

*error, typed load stage.* A quantity is a number in SI units, or a string holding a number and a unit from the fixed list (04 §7.1): `us ms s min h d`; `mm cm m km`; `ml L`; `g kg t`; `J kJ MJ GJ`; `W kW MW`; `N kN`; `Pa kPa MPa GPa`; `K C`; `m/s km/h`. A rate is a unit, or nothing, followed by `/s`, `/min`, `/h` or `/d`: `"0.012 kg/s"`, `"0.15 /h"`. Units are case-sensitive: `MJ` is a megajoule and `mJ` is not a unit.

<a id="e0205"></a>
## E0205 — A quantity has a unit of the wrong dimension for its field.

*error, typed load stage.* The unit is a real unit, but it measures something else than the field holds: a mass where a length belongs. The message names both dimensions and lists the units the field accepts.

<a id="e0206"></a>
## E0206 — A value is not one of the fixed set its field allows.

*error, typed load stage.* The field takes one of a fixed set of strings, and the value written is not among them. The message lists the set, and suggests the closest.

<a id="e0207"></a>
## E0207 — A value is of the right kind but is not acceptable.

*error, typed load stage.* The value could be read but the field's type refused it: a list of the wrong length, an empty string where a name is needed, a value its type cannot hold. The message carries the type's reason.

<a id="e0208"></a>
## E0208 — A number does not fit the field.

*error, typed load stage.* The field holds a whole number of limited size, and the number written is negative where only positive numbers fit, too large, or has a fraction.

<a id="e0301"></a>
## E0301 — A definition has no `type`.

*error, structure stage.* Every definition is an object with a `type` and an `id` (04 §5). `type` is a string naming the definition type: `"material"`, `"block"`.

<a id="e0302"></a>
## E0302 — A definition has no `id`.

*error, structure stage.* Every definition is an object with a `type` and an `id` (04 §5). `id` is a string: a bare name defines it in the mod's own namespace.

<a id="e0303"></a>
## E0303 — A definition's `type` is not a definition type the engine knows.

*error, structure stage.* Definition types are registered by the engine; data cannot add one. If a known type is close to the one written, the diagnostic suggests it.

<a id="e0304"></a>
## E0304 — An id does not have the required form.

*error, structure stage.* A qualified id is `namespace:name`, and a bare id is `name` (04 §4.1). Each part starts with a lowercase letter and holds only lowercase letters, digits and underscores.

<a id="e0305"></a>
## E0305 — An id is defined twice for the same definition type.

*error, structure stage.* Ids are unique per definition type (04 §4.1). Defining an id that already exists is an error that says where the first definition is. To change an existing definition use `"patch": true`; to replace it use `"override": true` (04 §6).

<a id="e0306"></a>
## E0306 — A mod defines an id in a namespace that is not its own.

*error, structure stage.* A mod may define new ids only in its own namespace (04 §4.2). An id qualified with another namespace is allowed only with `"patch": true` or `"override": true`, which change a definition that already exists. The namespace `engine` is reserved and can be neither defined in nor changed.

<a id="e0307"></a>
## E0307 — A patch names a definition that does not exist at that point.

*error, structure stage.* `"patch": true` changes an existing definition in place (04 §6.3). The definition must have been defined by a mod loaded earlier, or earlier in this mod. If the target is in another mod, list that mod in `requires` or `after` so that it loads first. If the target may legitimately be absent, add `"optional": true` and the patch is skipped when it is.

<a id="e0308"></a>
## E0308 — An override names a definition that does not exist at that point.

*error, structure stage.* `"override": true` replaces an existing definition (04 §6.4). The definition must have been defined by a mod loaded earlier, or earlier in this mod. To define something new, leave `override` out.

<a id="e0310"></a>
## E0310 — One of the keys every definition may carry has a wrong value.

*error, structure stage.* `abstract`, `patch`, `override`, `optional` and `obsolete` are `true` or `false`. `copy_from` is an id. `if_mod` and `unless_mod` are a mod id or a list of them. `extend`, `delete`, `scale` and `add` are objects whose keys are field paths. A definition cannot be both a patch and an override, and `optional` only means something on a patch.

<a id="e0401"></a>
## E0401 — `extend` cannot be applied.

*error, merge stage.* `"extend": { "tags": ["x"] }` appends to a list or set and merges into a map (04 §6.1). The value given must be a list when the field is a list and an object when the field is a map, and the field must be a list or a map.

<a id="e0402"></a>
## E0402 — `delete` cannot be applied.

*error, merge stage.* `"delete": { "tags": ["y"] }` removes entries from a list or set and keys from a map (04 §6.1). It takes a list: of values for a plain list, of entry ids for a list of objects with ids, of keys for a map. Deleting something that is not there is an error, because it usually means the thing was renamed and the patch no longer does what it was written to do.

<a id="e0403"></a>
## E0403 — `scale` cannot be applied.

*error, merge stage.* `"scale": { "density": 1.2 }` multiplies a number (04 §6.1). The factor must be a number, and the field must hold a number or a quantity with a unit. On a field the definition leaves out, `scale` acts on the field's default if the type declares one and is an error otherwise.

<a id="e0404"></a>
## E0404 — `add` cannot be applied.

*error, merge stage.* `"add": { "span": 2 }` adds to a number (04 §6.1). The amount must be a number or a quantity with a unit, of the same dimension as the field's value if that was written with a unit. On a field the definition leaves out, `add` acts on the field's default if the type declares one and is an error otherwise.

<a id="e0405"></a>
## E0405 — Definitions inherit from each other in a circle.

*error, merge stage.* `copy_from` gives a definition a parent (04 §6.2). If following parents comes back to where it started, none of them can be finished. The message names the definitions in the circle.

<a id="e0406"></a>
## E0406 — `copy_from` names a definition that does not exist.

*error, merge stage.* The parent of a definition must be a definition of the same type, in this mod or in a namespace it imports (04 §4.3, §6.2). It may be defined later or in another mod, and it may be abstract. If a definition of that type with a similar id exists, the diagnostic suggests it.

<a id="e0407"></a>
## E0407 — `copy_from` names a definition of another type.

*error, merge stage.* A definition inherits from one of the same type (04 §6.2): a block cannot copy from a material. The id written exists, but as another definition type.

<a id="e0408"></a>
## E0408 — A field path in `extend`, `delete`, `scale` or `add` leads nowhere.

*error, merge stage.* Keys inside `extend`, `delete`, `scale` and `add` may be dotted paths (04 §6.1). Each step names a key of an object, or the id of an entry in a list of objects that carry ids: `phases.windup.time`. The path given steps into something that is not an object or such a list, or names an entry that is not there.

<a id="e0409"></a>
## E0409 — `before` or `after` names a list entry that is not there.

*error, merge stage.* In a list of objects that carry ids, a new entry is appended unless it says `"before": id` or `"after": id` (04 §6.1). The id given is not the id of an entry in the list.

<a id="e0501"></a>
## E0501 — A reference names a definition that does not exist.

*error, link stage.* A bare name in a reference is looked up in the namespace of the mod that wrote it, then in each namespace that mod imports, in order (04 §4.3). A qualified reference is looked up exactly. Nothing of the expected type was found under the name. The diagnostic suggests the closest existing ids of that type.

<a id="e0502"></a>
## E0502 — A reference names an abstract definition.

*error, link stage.* A definition marked `"abstract": true` exists only to be inherited from. It is never instantiated and cannot be referred to except by `copy_from` (04 §5).

<a id="e0503"></a>
## E0503 — A reference is not written as an id.

*error, link stage.* A reference is a bare name or `namespace:name` (04 §4.1). Inline definitions have generated ids containing `#` and cannot be referred to from elsewhere (04 §5); give the inline definition an `id` of its own, or move it out to a definition of its own.

<a id="e0601"></a>
## E0601 — An expression holds a character that cannot start anything.

*error, compile stage.* Expressions are written in the language of 05 §4: names, numbers, texts in single quotation marks, operators and brackets. The caret is under a character that is none of those. A text is written 'like this'; a double quotation mark inside a JSON string would end the string.

<a id="e0602"></a>
## E0602 — A text in an expression has no closing quotation mark.

*error, compile stage.* A text in an expression starts and ends with a single quotation mark: 'ash'. A quotation mark inside the text is written twice: 'it''s'. The caret is at the mark that opened the text that never closed.

<a id="e0603"></a>
## E0603 — A number in an expression is malformed or too large.

*error, compile stage.* A whole number must fit in 64 bits. A number with a point needs a digit on both sides of it (`0.5`, not `.5`), and an exponent needs digits (`1e6`). There are no negative literals: `-5` is the negation of `5`.

<a id="e0604"></a>
## E0604 — A unit after a number in an expression is not one of the simple units.

*error, compile stage.* Inside an expression a number may be followed by a unit that is a scale: `us ms s min h d`, `mm cm m km`, `ml L`, `g kg t`, `J kJ MJ GJ`, `W kW MW`, `N kN`, `Pa kPa MPa GPa` and `K` (05 §4.7). Compound units such as `m/s` are written in JSON unit strings, and `C` is refused because it is an offset: `-5C` would read as minus 278.15.

<a id="e0605"></a>
## E0605 — An expression has something where the grammar expects something else.

*error, compile stage.* The expression could not be read by the grammar of 05 §4.1. The caret is under the first thing that does not fit, and the message says what was expected there. Common causes: two values with no operator between them, `=` for `==`, `&&` for `and`, a bracket that was never closed.

<a id="e0606"></a>
## E0606 — An expression ends where more is needed.

*error, compile stage.* The expression stops in the middle: after an operator, inside brackets, or after `if` without its `then` and `else`. The caret is at the end of what was written.

<a id="e0607"></a>
## E0607 — Two comparisons are written in a row.

*error, compile stage.* Comparisons do not chain: `a < b < c` would compare a boolean with a number. Write `a < b and b < c`.

<a id="e0608"></a>
## E0608 — A brace in a text template is not closed or not opened.

*error, compile stage.* In a text, anything in braces is an expression: "{the(self)} staggers back." (05 §4.6). A brace that is meant literally is written twice: `{{` and `}}`. The caret is under a `{` with no `}` after it, or a `}` with no `{` before it.

<a id="e0609"></a>
## E0609 — A number format in a text template is not `.N`.

*error, compile stage.* An expression in a text may be followed by a colon and a format: `{event.energy:.0}`. The format is a point and the number of digits to show after it, from 0 to 17, and nothing else.

<a id="e0610"></a>
## E0610 — An expression is too long or nested too deeply.

*error, compile stage.* So that nothing a mod writes can exhaust the compiler, brackets, `if`, `not` and unary minus nest at most 32 deep, a syntax tree is at most 100 operations deep, and a source string is at most 65,536 bytes (05 §4.1). Break the expression up with a function definition.

<a id="e0611"></a>
## E0611 — An expression has nothing in it.

*error, compile stage.* An expression field holds an empty string, or a text holds `{}`. Write the expression, or leave the field out if it has a default.

<a id="e0621"></a>
## E0621 — A name in an expression is not a subject bound where the expression appears.

*error, compile stage.* Each place an expression appears offers certain subjects by name: `self`, `target`, `here` and so on (05 §5.1, §7.3). The name under the caret is not one that this field offers. If a close name is bound, the diagnostic suggests it. A function is only a function where it is called: `clamp(…)`.

<a id="e0622"></a>
## E0622 — A `$name` is not a local or a parameter where the expression appears.

*error, compile stage.* `$name` reads a local variable or a parameter (05 §4.2). The field under the caret has no local of that name: a function sees only its own parameters, and a rule the locals defined before the expression runs.

<a id="e0623"></a>
## E0623 — A subject has no property of that name.

*error, compile stage.* `subject.name` reads a property of the subject's kind (05 §5.2). The kind of the subject under the caret has no property of that name; if a close one exists the diagnostic suggests it. A variable is read as `subject.var.name`.

<a id="e0624"></a>
## E0624 — An expression calls a function that does not exist.

*error, compile stage.* A bare function name is looked up among the engine's functions first, then in the mod's own namespace, then in each namespace it imports (05 §4.2). Nothing of the name under the caret was found. Functions defined by mods are `function` definitions (05 §12).

<a id="e0625"></a>
## E0625 — An expression reads an event field where there is no event or no such field.

*error, compile stage.* `event.name` reads a field of the event that triggered a rule (05 §4.2). Either the place this expression appears has no event, or the event has no field of that name. `event` is read one field at a time.

<a id="e0626"></a>
## E0626 — A text used as an id names no definition of that type.

*error, compile stage.* A text compared with an id, or written where an id is wanted, is resolved against the definitions of that type when mods load (05 §5.2): `here.block.material == 'glass'` is checked against the materials. The text under the caret names none of them. A bare name is looked up in the mod's own namespace and then in its imports.

<a id="e0628"></a>
## E0628 — An expression calls something that is neither a function nor a property.

*error, compile stage.* Only a function (`clamp(x, 0, 1)`) or a property that takes arguments (`here.field('fire')`) can be called. What is under the caret is a subject, a value or something else.

<a id="e0629"></a>
## E0629 — A variable is read on a kind of subject it is not declared on.

*error, compile stage.* A `variable` definition says what kind of thing the variable lives on: its `scope` (05 §6). The expression reads it from a subject of another kind, where it would never be found.

<a id="e0631"></a>
## E0631 — The target of an assignment cannot be assigned to.

*error, compile stage.* What `set` and `add` assign to is a place: a local (`$x`), a field of the event (`event.energy`), a variable (`self.var.kills`) or a settable property (`self.health`), optionally followed by keys (05 §10.3). What is under the caret is none of those.

<a id="e0641"></a>
## E0641 — An operator is given operands of types it does not accept.

*error, compile stage.* Arithmetic takes numbers, `+` also joins two texts or two lists, `and`, `or` and `not` take booleans, and `<` orders two numbers or two texts (05 §4.3). The message names the types that were found. To join a text with something else, turn it into a text with `str`.

<a id="e0642"></a>
## E0642 — A function or property is given the wrong number of arguments.

*error, compile stage.* The message shows the signature that was expected. Parameters marked with `?` may be left out, from the end.

<a id="e0643"></a>
## E0643 — An argument is of the wrong type.

*error, compile stage.* The argument under the caret does not have the type its parameter declares. The message shows the signature. An `int` is accepted where a `real` is wanted, and not the other way round: use `floor`, `ceil` or `round`.

<a id="e0645"></a>
## E0645 — An expression's type is not the one its field wants.

*error, compile stage.* Each expression field declares the type of value it wants (05 §7.1): a condition wants a boolean, a duration a number. The expression under the caret gives something else. The message names both types.

<a id="e0646"></a>
## E0646 — A comparison is between types that can never be equal or ordered.

*error, compile stage.* `==` compares numbers with numbers, texts with texts, an id with an id of the same type or with a text, and subjects with subjects (05 §4.3). The two sides here can never be equal, so the comparison would always be false: one of them is not what was meant.

<a id="e0647"></a>
## E0647 — An index is applied to something that is not a list or a map.

*error, compile stage.* `xs[i]` reads an element of a list, counting from zero, and `m['key']` an entry of a map (05 §4.3). What is under the caret is neither.

<a id="e0648"></a>
## E0648 — A property is read from a value that is not a subject or a map.

*error, compile stage.* `value.name` reads a property of a subject or an entry of a map. A number, a text, a boolean or a list has neither. If the value is an id, read the definition through the subject it came from.

<a id="e0661"></a>
## E0661 — A random function is used where the value must be pure.

*error, compile stage.* Some fields must give the same answer every time they are asked: what a screen shows, a preview, a sorting key (05 §7.3). Random functions (`rand`, `chance`, `pick`, …), a `pick` value source and any function definition that uses one are refused there.

<a id="e0662"></a>
## E0662 — A character's decision reads something the character could not know.

*error, compile stage.* Goals, methods, tactics, an action's defaults and ordinary screens are compiled in the mind context (05 §7.3): they may read the character's own state, what it has perceived and whatever is registered as safe for belief. The read under the caret is ground truth about something else (01 R11). Read what the character has perceived instead (15 §7). A function definition is safe for belief only if everything it reads is.

<a id="e0671"></a>
## E0671 — A type name is not a type.

*error, compile stage.* A function's `params` and `returns` and a variable's `value` name types as the language writes them (05 §3): `bool`, `int`, `real`, `number`, `string`, `any`, a kind of subject such as `entity`, `id<material>`, `list<int>`, `map<real>`, and any of those followed by `?` for one that may be null.

<a id="e0672"></a>
## E0672 — A function always calls itself.

*error, compile stage.* Functions may call each other, and themselves, to a fixed depth (05 §12). This one calls itself, directly or through others, on every path through its body, so it could never finish. Put the call inside an `if … then … else`, or after `and`, `or` or `??`, so that there is a case in which it is not made.

<a id="e0673"></a>
## E0673 — A function definition is not well formed.

*error, compile stage.* A function's parameters are named like locals: letters, digits and underscores, not starting with a digit, each name once. A parameter with a `default` may be left out when the function is called, so those come last, and a default is a constant. A function defined in place inside another definition has no name to be called by.

<a id="e0674"></a>
## E0674 — A variable declaration is not well formed.

*error, compile stage.* A `variable` definition names the kind of thing it lives on in `scope` (`entity`, `cell`, `site`, `global`, …) and its type in `value` (05 §6). Its `default`, if it has one, is a constant of that type; without one the variable reads as null until it is set.

<a id="e0675"></a>
## E0675 — A definition type declares a scope the registry cannot supply.

*error, compile stage.* Each expression field says what is in scope there, by the names of kinds, types and events (04 §7.3). One of those names is not registered. This is a mistake in the engine or in how the tool was started, not in the mod: the loader was given a registry without the kinds this definition type needs.

<a id="e0676"></a>
## E0676 — A value source is not well formed.

*error, compile stage.* Where an expression string cannot say a value, an object can (05 §7.4): `{ "expr": "…" }`, `{ "call": "function", "args": { … } }`, or a query under `count`, `collect`, `first`, `pick`, `sum`, `min` or `max`. A `call` names a function definition and gives its arguments by parameter name.

<a id="e0677"></a>
## E0677 — A query is not well formed.

*error, compile stage.* A query is an object with one key, the kind of query, whose value holds its arguments and `where`, `sort` and `limit` (05 §11): `{ "entities": { "around": "self", "radius": 12, "where": "…" } }`. The kinds are `list`, `defs` and those the engine registers (`entities`, `cells`, `contents`, `areas`, `sites`). A spatial query takes at most one shape, and `radius` goes with `around`. The message says what is unknown, missing or misplaced.

<a id="e0678"></a>
## E0678 — A query covers more cells than a query may.

*error, compile stage.* A spatial query's extent is capped by `rules.max_query_cells`, 1,048,576 cells unless set (05 §11, §13.2). This one's size is known when the mod loads, and it is larger than that. A radius covers a box of cells round its centre, a storey counting three metres. Narrow it with a smaller radius, a `box` or `in_area`.

<a id="e0681"></a>
## E0681 — An effect names nothing that can be done.

*error, compile stage.* An effect is an object with one key, its verb (05 §10.1): one of the effects of 05 §10.2 to §10.5, a verb a subsystem registered, or a rule that takes parameters. Nothing of the name under the caret was found. A rule is looked up in the mod's own namespace and then in each namespace it imports; one with no `params` is run with `{ "run": "its_id" }`.

<a id="e0682"></a>
## E0682 — An effect is not well formed.

*error, compile stage.* Each effect takes its arguments in a fixed form (05 §10): a verb takes them by name in an object, or its one obvious argument directly; `if` takes `then` and `else`; a loop takes `do`. The message says what is missing, unknown or misplaced, and shows what the effect takes.

<a id="e0683"></a>
## E0683 — An effect is used where it has no meaning.

*error, compile stage.* `return` gives a value to whoever called a rule, so it is written in a rule and nowhere else. `modify`, `cancel_event` and `consume` act on the event a rule is handling: `modify` and `cancel_event` only in a rule that listens for a hook, and `modify` only on a field the hook declares mutable (05 §8.2, §10.5). A `run` or `emit` whose result is wanted is written as the value of a `let`.

<a id="e0684"></a>
## E0684 — A rule, a rule group or a reason is not well formed.

*error, compile stage.* A rule names the event it listens for in `on`, which must be registered; `as` and `filter` name a subject and fields of that event; `params` are named like locals, and those with a default come last; `returns` and the kinds in `subjects` are types as the language writes them (05 §9). A reason's `values` are named like locals and typed the same way (14 §15).

<a id="e0701"></a>
## E0701 — A definition was read but breaks one of its type's own rules.

*error, semantic stage.* Each definition type checks what cannot be expressed as the kind of a single field: ranges, fields that exclude each other, limits (04 §8.1). The message is the type's own.

<a id="e0802"></a>
## E0802 — A mod uses an experimental feature it has not opted in to.

*error, cross stage.* An experimental feature is specified so that it can be tried. It may change incompatibly or be removed (04 §8.4). A mod that uses one must name the feature in the `experimental` list of its `mod.json`. The message says which feature and where it is used.

<a id="e0902"></a>
## E0902 — A broken definition cannot be replaced by a placeholder.

*error, lenient stage.* `--lenient` replaces each broken definition with a placeholder (04 §8.3), but this definition type does not supply one, so loading cannot carry on past it. Fix the definition.

<a id="n0901"></a>
## N0901 — A broken definition was replaced by a placeholder.

*note, lenient stage.* With `--lenient`, each definition that could not be loaded is replaced by an inert placeholder of its type and loading carries on (04 §8.3). The errors are still reported. This is for working on a large mod with something temporarily broken; the result is not fit to play or to save from.

<a id="w0010"></a>
## W0010 — A mod's directory is not named after its id.

*warning, mods stage.* A mod lives in `mods/<mod_id>/` (04 §3.1). The mod loads under the id in its `mod.json` whatever the directory is called, but a directory with another name is hard to find from an error message. Rename the directory.

<a id="w0011"></a>
## W0011 — A mod is hidden by one with the same id in an earlier search directory.

*warning, mods stage.* Mods are looked for in each search directory in turn, and the first directory that holds a given id supplies it (04 §3.1). A copy in a later directory is ignored. This is how a working copy in the user's directory replaces an installed mod; if it is not intended, remove one.

<a id="w0410"></a>
## W0410 — Two mods replace the same field with different values.

*warning, cross stage.* Two mods that `scale`, `add` to or `extend` a field compose. Two mods that replace it do not: the later wins, silently undoing the earlier (04 §6.3). If the later mod knows of the earlier and means to win, it says so by listing the earlier in its `requires` or `after`, and the warning goes away.

<a id="w0504"></a>
## W0504 — A bare reference matches in more than one imported namespace.

*warning, link stage.* A bare name is looked up in the mod's own namespace and then in each import in order, and the first match wins (04 §4.3). The name also exists in a later namespace, so which definition is meant depends on the order of `imports`. Write the reference qualified, `namespace:name`, to be clear.

<a id="w0627"></a>
## W0627 — An expression reads a variable that no definition declares.

*warning, compile stage.* Using an undeclared variable works, and is reported because a misspelt variable name that silently creates a new variable is the commonest mistake in rules (05 §6). Declare it with a `variable` definition. A mod with `"strict_vars": true` in its `mod.json` makes this an error for everything it writes.

<a id="w0630"></a>
## W0630 — A bare name in an expression is found in more than one namespace.

*warning, compile stage.* A bare name is looked up in the mod's own namespace and then in each namespace it imports, and the first match wins (04 §4.3). Another namespace on the list has the same name, so a change in load order or in an import could change what is meant. Write the name with its namespace.

<a id="w0644"></a>
## W0644 — A value that may be null is used where a value is needed.

*warning, compile stage.* Things go missing: a target dies, a variable was never set (05 §4.4). The compiler can see that what is under the caret may be null, and arithmetic with null gives null and a warning every time it runs. Give a value for that case with `??`: `target.mass ?? 0`.

<a id="w0649"></a>
## W0649 — An operation on constants fails every time it runs.

*warning, compile stage.* The compiler can see that an operation such as `1 / 0` cannot succeed. It is left as written, gives null and warns each time it runs (05 §4.5).

<a id="w0690"></a>
## W0690 — While running, a query was refused.

*warning, run time stage.* A query whose size could not be known when the mod loaded turned out to cover more than `rules.max_query_cells` cells, or was given arguments its kind cannot use: a shape that is nowhere, two shapes, a radius below zero (05 §11). It had no results, and a value source over it gave null.

<a id="w0691"></a>
## W0691 — While running, arithmetic met a null.

*warning, run time stage.* A value was needed and what arrived was null: a target that no longer exists, a variable that was never set, a property of something that is not loaded (05 §4.4). The operation gave null. Give a value for that case with `??`.

<a id="w0692"></a>
## W0692 — While running, a number was divided by zero.

*warning, run time stage.* Division by zero gives null and this warning (05 §4.5). Test the divisor first, or give the result a fallback with `??`.

<a id="w0693"></a>
## W0693 — While running, a function was given a number it has no answer for.

*warning, run time stage.* The square root of a negative number, the logarithm of a number that is not positive and the like give null and this warning (05 §4.5). The message says which.

<a id="w0694"></a>
## W0694 — While running, integer arithmetic left the range of a 64-bit integer.

*warning, run time stage.* The result would not fit, so the operation gave null (05 §4.5). Use real numbers for quantities that large.

<a id="w0695"></a>
## W0695 — While running, a value had a type the operation does not accept.

*warning, run time stage.* This can only happen where the type was `any` when the mod loaded: an undeclared variable, a parameter typed `any`. The operation gave null. Declare the variable or the parameter with its type and the mistake is found at load.

<a id="w0696"></a>
## W0696 — While running, a list, a map or a text grew past the size limit.

*warning, run time stage.* One value may hold at most `rules.max_value_size` elements, or bytes of text (05 §13.2). The operation that would have passed the limit gave null.

<a id="w0697"></a>
## W0697 — While running, a random function had no stream to draw from.

*warning, run time stage.* Random functions draw from a stream the simulation supplies. This evaluation had none, which is how the engine evaluates a field that must be pure, so the function gave null.

<a id="w0698"></a>
## W0698 — While running, functions called each other too deeply.

*warning, run time stage.* A function definition may call itself, directly or through others, to a fixed depth: `rules.max_call_depth`, 32 unless set (05 §12, §13.2). The call that would have gone deeper was refused and gave null. Check the case that is meant to end the recursion.

<a id="w0699"></a>
## W0699 — While running, something was asked for that the engine does not offer yet.

*warning, run time stage.* The value source was read and kept when the mod loaded, and what it needs is not built in this version of the engine. It gave null. The message says what is missing.

<a id="w0702"></a>
## W0702 — A definition is valid but probably not what was meant.

*warning, semantic stage.* Each definition type may warn of what is allowed and usually a mistake. The message is the type's own.

<a id="w0801"></a>
## W0801 — An abstract definition is never inherited from.

*warning, cross stage.* A definition marked `"abstract": true` exists only as a parent for `copy_from` (04 §5). Nothing copies from this one, so it has no effect. Remove it, or check the `copy_from` that was meant to name it.

<a id="w0803"></a>
## W0803 — A mod relies on an experimental feature.

*warning, cross stage.* The mod names an experimental feature in its `mod.json` (04 §8.4). This warning is given at every load, by name, as a reminder that the feature may change incompatibly or be removed, and that a save records which experimental features its mods used.

## The expression compiler

What the compiler finds in an expression; the loader reports each under a code of group `06` (04 §8.2). `X9..` are warnings while an expression runs (05 §4.5).

| Code | Means |
|------|-------|
| `X101` | a character that cannot start any token |
| `X102` | a string with no closing quote |
| `X103` | a number that is malformed or too large |
| `X104` | a unit after a number that is not one of the simple units |
| `X105` | a token where the grammar expects something else |
| `X106` | the expression ends where more is needed |
| `X107` | two comparisons in a row; comparisons do not chain |
| `X108` | a brace in a text template that is not closed or not opened |
| `X109` | a number format in a text template that is not `.N` |
| `X110` | an expression that is too long or nested too deeply |
| `X111` | an expression with nothing in it |
| `X201` | a name that is not a subject bound in this context |
| `X202` | a `$name` that is not a local of this context |
| `X203` | a property the subject's kind does not have |
| `X204` | a function that is not registered |
| `X205` | an event field where there is no event or no such field |
| `X206` | a text used as an id that names no definition of that type |
| `X207` | a variable that no definition declares |
| `X208` | a call of something that is neither a function nor a property |
| `X209` | a variable read on a kind of subject it is not declared on |
| `X210` | a bare name found in more than one imported namespace |
| `X211` | the target of an assignment that cannot be assigned to |
| `X301` | operands whose types the operator does not accept |
| `X302` | the wrong number of arguments |
| `X303` | an argument of the wrong type |
| `X304` | a value that may be null used in arithmetic |
| `X305` | the expression's type is not the one the field wants |
| `X306` | a comparison between types that can never be equal or ordered |
| `X307` | an index into something that is not a list or a map |
| `X308` | a property read on a value that is not a subject or a map |
| `X309` | an operation on constants that fails every time |
| `X401` | a random function where the context must be pure |
| `X402` | a read that is not safe for belief, in a mind context |
| `X901` | run time: arithmetic met a null |
| `X902` | run time: division by zero |
| `X903` | run time: a function was given a number outside its domain |
| `X904` | run time: integer arithmetic overflowed |
| `X905` | run time: a value had a type the operation does not accept |
| `X906` | run time: a list, a map or a text grew past the size limit |
| `X907` | run time: a random function was called with no stream |
| `X908` | run time: functions called each other deeper than calls may nest |
| `X909` | run time: something was asked for that the engine does not offer yet |
| `X910` | run time: a query was refused |

## The console and test scripts

What the console finds in a command or a test script (14 §3, §7).

| Code | Means |
|------|-------|
| `E1401` | a character appears where no value can start or continue |
| `E1402` | a quote is opened and never closed |
| `E1403` | inside double quotes a backslash may only come before a double quote or another backslash |
| `E1404` | JSON in braces runs to its closing brace, which is missing |
| `E1405` | what the braces hold is not valid JSON |
| `E1406` | a reference is @here, @self, @sel, @c:x,y,z, @e:id, @kind:name or a name given with as= |
| `E1407` | `key=` must be followed directly by a value |
| `E1408` | a line starts with a command name, after an optional `as <reference>` |
| `E1409` | two values need a space between them |
| `E1410` | a console line is at most 65,536 bytes |
| `E1411` | a bracket opened inside an unquoted value is never closed |
| `E1421` | no command has this name |
| `E1422` | the command has no parameter with this name |
| `E1423` | a required argument was not given |
| `E1424` | more positional arguments were given than the command takes |
| `E1425` | an argument was given more than once |
| `E1426` | a value is not of the type its parameter takes |
| `E1427` | the command is not offered by the host it was typed in |
| `E1428` | an expression does not parse |
| `E1429` | a name given with as= is letters, digits and underscores, and not a reserved reference |
| `E1441` | an expectation is `expect event`, `expect trace`, `expect reason`, `expect hash` or `expect frame` |
| `E1442` | a state hash is 32 hexadecimal digits |
